paragraph: The Simplifica programmes of 2021 and 2023 [put certificates, registrations, authorisations and licences on www.sepe.gov.ao](<https://doi.org/10.22533/at.ed.216532523063>). In the last twelve months the SEPE portal was cited and not changed. In October 2026 Portal de T.I. reported that [the SEPE portal is online and working, with registration, sign-in and a catalogue of services](<https://pti.ao/sepe-mantem-servicos-online-e-acessiveis-ao-publico/>). In November 2026 the migration service [moved border-visa applications fully online for registered entities](<https://www.diario94.com/noticia/sme-digitaliza-pedidos-de-visto-de-fronteira-em-angola-621c>). No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online. None says that one account reaches several ministries' services, or counts users of SEPE. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In July 2026 the Burundi Revenue Office said [the land tax declaration for 2026/2027 must be filed online on its UMUTANGAKORI II platform](<https://www.obr.bi/index.php/communiques/2612-communique-declaration-et-paiement-en-ligne-de-l-impot-foncier>). The deadline was 30 September 2026. Since 6 May 2024 the urban planning office has [taken building-permit applications online](<https://burundi-eco.com/le-permis-de-construire-digitalise/>), Burundi Eco reports. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the World Bank listed [a tender for a national e-Gouv portal](<https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/procurement-detail/OP00476457>) under the PAFEN project. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online. None says that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In November 2026 [service-public.bj listed 1,208 services, 131 of them available online](<https://www.nasuba.info/politique-societe/benin-comment-fonctionne-le-portail-numerique-des-services-publics/>), by its own count. [Users of service-public.bj create an account or sign in to a personal space](<https://www.nasuba.info/politique-societe/benin-comment-fonctionne-le-portail-numerique-des-services-publics/>). [Over 50 institutions offer services through the portal](<https://cyber.ee/resources/news/cybernetica-and-benin-continue-enhancing-the-country-s-digitalisation/>), Cybernetica said in February 2025. In the last twelve months, since 1 November 2026, [a criminal record certificate is issued at once on the portal](<https://beninwebtv.bj/en/digitization-in-benin-criminal-records-now-issued-instantly-and-without-supporting-documents/>). On 18 November 2026 the digital minister [said Benin had deployed more than 250 e-services](<https://techcabal.com/2026/11/20/afrilabs-2026-benin-innovation/>). In November 2026 [the portal showed more than 2.5 million requests](<https://www.nasuba.info/politique-societe/benin-comment-fonctionne-le-portail-numerique-des-services-publics/>).

On 5 May 2026 the government [launched service-public.gov.bf to bring public services online in one place](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burkina-faso-launches-central-portal-to-streamline-e-services>). The portal [offers 95 procedures completed online and links 183 public institutions](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burkina-faso-launches-central-portal-to-streamline-e-services>). In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the government [launched version 2 of the Service Public BF portal](<https://service-public.gov.bf/actualites/lancement-du-portail-service-public-bf-v2>). In December 2025 [three justice platforms opened](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0201-51743-burkina-faso-to-step-up-justice-system-digitalisation-this-year>) for complaints, prison visit permits and commercial registry papers. No source found says how users sign in to the portal, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

In February 2026 the 2026/27 budget [confirmed continued investment in the platform](<https://www.bwtechzone.com/2026/02/botswana-doubles-down-on-digital.html>), which the government calls its integrated e-services platform, 1Gov1Citizen. In the last twelve months the budget speech [put 52 public services fully online on the 1Gov1Citizen platform](<https://www.bwtechzone.com/2026/02/botswana-doubles-down-on-digital.html>), BWTechZone reports. A further 179 services were then in final integration testing. A 2023 review [found the earlier 1Gov portal unstable, poorly linked to agencies and little used](<https://www.adm.ee/blog/case-study-botswana-1gov-platform-assessment/>), ADM Interactive says. No source found says how users sign in to 1Gov1Citizen, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

On 14 October 2026 the government [launched a national digital portal for public services](<https://africabusinessinsight.com/central-african-republics-digital-public-services-face-connectivity-barriers/>), Africa Business Insight reports. On it people can apply for driving licences and urban transport passes, request criminal record extracts and nationality certificates, and obtain school attendance and baccalaureate certificates. The portal [carries services of the transport, justice and education sectors](<https://africabusinessinsight.com/central-african-republics-digital-public-services-face-connectivity-barriers/>). It is the one change in the last twelve months that has been found. No source found says how users sign in to it, or that ten or more services can be completed on it. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

SNDI, the state IT company, said [315 administrative procedures had been digitised and put online by 31 December 2025](<https://ivoirexpress.ci/2026/07/28/digitalisation-des-services-publics-en-cote-divoire-les-applications-metiers-developpees-par-la-sndi/>). They are on the national public services portal. In May 2025 the trade ministry said the GUCE-CI single window [lets businesses complete import, export and transit formalities online](<https://www.commerce.gouv.ci/actualite/133>). In the last twelve months, on 10 November 2026, the tourism ministry [opened a digital one-stop shop for tourism operators](<https://www.linfodrome.com/societe/127482-administration-touristique-les-operateurs-pourront-desormais-effectuer-leurs-demarches-en-ligne>). They file procedures, pay and track applications online, first in four regional offices. No source found says how users sign in to the national portal. None counts its users. Operating would need one national portal that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

In August 2023 the finance ministry [unveiled Tresor Pay for paying non-tax public services online](<https://cameroonnewsagency.com/government-modernizes-revenue-collection-system-with-the-introduction-of-tresor-pay-platform/>), by mobile money, post office or card. In the last twelve months, in August 2026, the tax directorate launched [registrations.dgi.cm for registering deeds online](<https://lefisk.cm/blog/enregistrement-actes-en-ligne-dgi-cameroun-registrations-guide>). Three public procurement acts could be registered and paid for by mobile money. More than 120 other acts in its catalogue were shown as unavailable. No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In June 2026 the government [launched RDC-Pass, a national digital identity platform, in Kinshasa](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202606/drc-launches-rdc-pass-digital-id-platform-under-20-year-ppp-with-trident>). Its rollout began with pilot testing. In the last twelve months, on 19 November 2026, the civil service ministry [announced E-Services RDC, a portal and app publishing the procedures and official fees of public services](<https://acp.cd/nation/rdc-le-gouvernement-annonce-la-creation-de-la-plateforme-numerique-e-services-rdc/>) in six languages. In July 2026 the business one-stop shop GUCE [presented a site that tracks company files in real time and an app for formalising informal operators](<https://actualite.cd/2026/07/28/formalisation-des-entreprises-en-rdc-daniel-mukoko-samba-mise-sur-le-numerique-pour>). No source found names a ministry service that users reach through RDC-Pass, or says that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

The digital economy ministry says citizens can use the e-Citizen Portal [to file administrative procedures, pay taxes and fees, and track their files in real time](<https://numerique.gouv.cg/actualites/architecture-et-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi>). The ministry [describes the e-Citizen Portal as the single entry point to all digital public services](<https://numerique.gouv.cg/actualites/architecture-et-digital-public-infrastructure-dpi>). In June 2024 the budget ministry [reviewed E-Bourses, a project to let students apply online for scholarships](<https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/gouvernance-le-ministere-du-budget-temoigne-la-bonne-execution-de-trois-projets-157749>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, and no count of users has been found. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In June 2024 the national digital agency ANADEN [held a technical meeting to present e-Bourse, a national portal for online scholarship applications](<https://anaden.org/realisations>). ANADEN lists the portal among its projects and marks it as in progress. In June 2025 its procurement notice [listed an upgraded government portal with e-services and digital payments](<https://www.afdb.org/sites/default/files/documents/project-related-procurement/agpm_padec-comores_180625.pdf>), funded by the AfDB. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says that one national portal carries several ministries' services, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

On 18 December 2024 the government [launched the Portal de Justiça](<https://www.governo.cv/primeiro-ministro-preside-acto-de-lancamento-oficial-do-portal-de-justica/>). Users of the Portal de Justiça [sign in through Autentika, the state's authentication platform](<https://www.governo.cv/primeiro-ministro-preside-acto-de-lancamento-oficial-do-portal-de-justica/>). In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the government launched [Gov.cv, a single portal for public services](<https://caboverde24.info/en/2026/07/22/ja-sabe-como-aceder-aos-servicos-publicos-sem-sair-de-casa-analisamos-o-site/>). It takes criminal record, nationality and higher education applications and tracks each request. No source found says how users sign in to Gov.cv, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether government services can be used online in Djibouti. No source found names a services portal or app, or a service that can be applied for or paid online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government services portal or app launched, or a service piloted that can be applied for or paid online.

In July 2026 the High Commission for Digitalisation said [the national portal, Dzair Digital Services, carried 21 digital services](<https://elhiwar.dz/event/335541/>), with 62 planned by the end of 2027. In the last twelve months the count has risen. By 10 November 2026 [the portal offered 68 services](<https://www.echoroukonline.com/portail-numerique-les-documents-en-ligne-desormais-reconnus>). On 19 November 2026 a High Commission for Digitalisation expert [put it at 91 public services](<https://news.radioalgerie.dz/ar/node/99407>). [Twenty tourism and handicraft services were added on 16 November](<https://www.algerie360.com/dzair-digital-services-tourisme-artisanat-nouveaux-services/>). The expert said [one account reaches services of the interior, local government, employment, social security, tax and justice sectors](<https://news.radioalgerie.dz/ar/node/99407>). On 19 November 2026 the expert [gave about two million registered citizens and nearly 11 million visits](<https://news.radioalgerie.dz/ar/node/99407>).

In September 2026 communications minister Raafat Hindy said [the Digital Egypt platform provides more than 240 government services in 29 bundles](<https://www.alnaharegypt.com/1196568>). In the last twelve months the stated count has risen. In November 2026 the assistant minister [put the count at 261 services in 29 packages](<https://cairoict.com/news/prime-minister-opens-the-30th-cairo-ict-as-egypt-sets-out-its-ai-targets>), plus 21 apps. Enterprise reports that [one Digital Egypt account, opened with the 14-digit national ID and a mobile number](<https://enterpriseam.com/egypt/2026/08/02/your-guide-to-navigating-egypts-online-government-services/>), works across civil status, traffic, real estate and court services. In October 2026 an assistant minister said [Digital Egypt had about 13.5 million users](<https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/8381060>). In November 2026 the ministry put [active users at 13.7 million, up from 10.4 million a year earlier](<https://cairoict.com/news/prime-minister-opens-the-30th-cairo-ict-as-egypt-sets-out-its-ai-targets>). Transactions rose from 23.8 million to 36 million.

On 24 September 2024 the Eritrean embassy in the United States [launched the Consular Affairs Processing System (CAPS)](<https://us.embassyeritrea.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/09-19-2024_Announcement-Launching-CAPS-to-Public-Englsih-Final.pdf>). The foreign ministry built it. Through CAPS, applications for ID cards, entry visas and passport renewals are begun online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No other government service in Eritrea has been found online since October 2023, and no source found says whether a national portal exists. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

[National ID Ethiopia's May 2026 deck calls MESOB a digital one-stop shop for e-government services built on the Fayda ID](<https://id4africa.com/2026/files/T1-2-1-Ethiopia-FINAL.pdf>). Prime Minister Abiy [inaugurated the Unified MESOB Application, which brings 27 services from several institutions onto one platform](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_9070888>). In the last twelve months, on 30 March 2026, Ethio Telecom launched teleSign, where people [apply online for document authentication, powers of attorney and professional licences, paid by telebirr](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_8578538>). In October 2026 the trade ministry said [1,088,787 business registration and licensing services were delivered online in three months](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_9819771>). No source found gives users, applications or transactions through a national portal. Mature would need a number of users, applications or transactions through the national portal published.

In November 2023 the immigration directorate DGDI [opened an e-services portal](<https://techies.ga/article/la-dgdi-lance-un-portail-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives>) for renewing passports, ID cards and residence permits. In the last twelve months the Gabon Connect platform [was set up in March 2026 to put tax, customs, land and social security procedures online](<https://gabonmediatime.com/gabon-connect-le-ministere-de-leconomie-sollicite-lexpertise-de-lapdpvp/>). On 22 October 2026 the vice-president of the government [presented Gabon Connect as a single digital window](<https://www.gabonreview.com/gabon-connect-tresorpay-dus-le-gabon-mise-sur-le-numerique-pour-mieux-encaisser/>), with a first phase due to finish in December 2027. On 16 November 2026 the state pension fund CPPF [launched its Baana platform nationwide](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-prestations-familiales-mouila-la-cppf-sensibilise-les-agents-publics-au-nouveau-mode-de-gestion-des-certificats-de-scolarite/>). No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or counts users of a national portal. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

The Interior Ministry [opened an online services portal, fully working from 15 December 2025](<https://www.graphic.com.gh/news/general-news/ghana-news-interior-ministry-launches-online-digital-services-portal.html>). It takes applications for immigrant quota permits, citizenship renunciation, dual nationality, naturalisation and licences. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the Lands Commission's portal [let buyers pay for a land search and receive the report by email](<https://www.citinewsroom.com/2026/10/lands-commission-outlines-four-steps-for-conducting-online-land-searches/>), live in 10 of 16 regions. The digital economy policy [describes Ghana.gov as the portal that centralises access to government services](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Ghana-Digital-Economy-Policy-Strategy.pdf>). No source found counts ten or more services online, or says how users sign in to Ghana.gov. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

On 7 May 2026 the minister [launched the deployment of the national e-Services platform](<https://ande.gov.gn/rencontre-du-ministre-avec-lequipe-e-services-vers-le-lancement-de-e-services-une-solution-innovante-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives/>), built inside the digital agency ANDE. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the livestock ministry [launched Ngaynaako, a portal for livestock requests](<https://laguinee.info/2026/10/22/guinee-le-ministere-de-lelevage-lance-ngaynaako-son-guichet-unique-numerique/>). On 26 October 2026 the fisheries ministry [launched Konkoe, where fishers apply for licences and track their files](<https://guineenews.org/2026/10/26/peche-la-guinee-lance-le-sigpem-pour-simplifier-les-demarches-administratives/>). No source found says that ten or more services can be completed online, or that one national portal carries several ministries' services with one sign-in. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In September 2024 the minister said [the government was building a one-stop platform for its services](<https://standard.gm/dr-ceesay-says-govt-committed-to-building-capacities/>). In 2025 the communications ministry [presented MYGOV, a one-stop platform starting with five pilot services](<https://publicadministration.desa.un.org/sites/default/files/list-of-files/2025/1.2.1%29%20data%20governance%20-mocde.pdf>), modelled on Bangladesh's platform, with UNDP and ECOWAS support. In 2025 the National Records Commission [opened a portal for information requests](<https://informationcommission.gm/en/news/3923befe-e60f-4ba7-8369-95f1f7ca7059>), tracked online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says that MYGOV is in service, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether government services can be used online in Guinea-Bissau. No source found names a services portal or app, or a service that can be applied for or paid online. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a government services portal or app launched, or a service piloted that can be applied for or paid online.

Equatorial Guinea's [e-visa service opened on 1 July 2023](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_gobierno_analiza_el_contrato_de_vfs_global_para_reforzar_el_sistema_de_visados_en_linea_y_potenciar_la_promocion_turistica>), run for the government by the company VFS Global. In the last twelve months, in July 2026, the document agency CNEDOGE [put requests for official documents online](<https://farolegnoticias.com/cnedoge-habilita-la-solicitud-de-documentos-oficiales-en-linea-y-avanza-en-la-digitalizacion-de-los-servicios-publicos/>), with payment notes and status tracking. In October 2026 the Vice-President [said it had processed about 35,127 e-visas since its launch](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_gobierno_analiza_el_contrato_de_vfs_global_para_reforzar_el_sistema_de_visados_en_linea_y_potenciar_la_promocion_turistica>), against 200,000 a year expected. No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, or names a single national portal. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In October 2024 the Treasury Cabinet Secretary [told the Senate the platform carried 16,000 services, up from 397](<https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/economy/state-collects-sh127bn-via-e-citizen-4784244>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026, the ICT Cabinet Secretary [said more than 22,500 services were available on eCitizen](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/7426/>). The draft 2026 Budget Policy Statement [put services onboarded at over 17,668, from more than 350 agencies](<https://radiogeneration.co.ke/news/110840/ecitizen-under-scrutiny-over-sh365bn-collections-gap>). In December 2024 eCitizen's Director General [put active accounts at 13.5 million](<https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/realtime/2024-12-27-state-collects-sh900m-per-day-on-ecitizen-as-users-hit-135-million>). A May 2026 government presentation [gave over 15 million active eCitizen accounts](<https://id4africa.com/2026/files/T1-1-3-Kenya-FINAL.pdf>). No count of transactions through eCitizen in 2026 has been found.

[The Liberia Revenue Authority says it launched an Online Duty-Free Application Platform in July 2025](<https://revenue.lra.gov.lr/lra-digitizes-rural-customs-offices-rolls-out-online-duty-free-platform/>). In the last twelve months, in November 2026, [the consulate general in New York put payment for all consular services online](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/liberias-new-york-consulate-introduces-online-payment-for-services/>), among them visas and passports. The mines ministry's deputy minister said [its online system for mining licence applications was fully operational](<https://www.liberianobserver.com/news/mme-trains-certifies-geologists-mining-consultancy-firms-on-licensing-procedures/article_0216311d-d201-42e2-b3c4-c0080794ab97.html>). No source found since October 2023 says that ten or more services can be completed online, names a single gateway with national ID sign-in, or publishes a portal's use. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

On 3 March 2024 the Government of National Unity's interior ministry [launched a package of e-services](<https://alwasat.ly/news/libya/431469>), including the start of an e-government portal project. In December 2024 [Cabinet Decision 705 created the Dawlati platform](<https://lawsociety.ly/legislation/%d9%82%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%b1-%d9%85%d8%ac%d9%84%d8%b3-%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%88%d8%b2%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%a1-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-705-%d9%84%d8%b3%d9%86%d8%a9-2024-%d9%85-%d8%a8%d8%b4%d8%a3%d9%86-%d8%a5%d9%86%d8%b4/>) to provide e-services and issue official documents. In the last twelve months, in late October 2026, the passports authority's [e-visa unit received 773 applications in a week and approved 610](<https://lana.gov.ly/post.php?id=368841&lang=ar>). No source found says whether a national portal is in service, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

In June 2024 UNDP and the communications ministry [launched the E-Service Outlet Model](<https://www.undp.org/lesotho/news/undp-launched-e-service-outlet-model>). Under it, internet and print shops and mobile money agents help people use government e-services. In the last twelve months, in May 2026, a minister said [an integrated online services platform with a payment gateway was close to launch](<https://lestimes.com/?p=90492>). Also in May 2026 the ministry [validated the first stage of automating e-services with Home Affairs, Public Service, Public Works and Finance](<https://www.gov.ls/ict/lesotho-eservices-to-undergo-evolution-as-part-of-digital-transformation-agenda/>). No source found says the platform has launched, that one sign-in reaches several ministries, or that ten or more services can be completed online. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

On 18 September 2026 the digital transition ministry [relaunched the national Idarati portal](<https://fr.assahafa.com/lancement-de-la-nouvelle-version-du-portail-national-idarati-pour-une-administration-plus-proche-et-plus-intelligente/>). The ministry says [Idarati gives access to 874 online services and 2,533 published administrative acts](<https://fr.assahafa.com/lancement-de-la-nouvelle-version-du-portail-national-idarati-pour-une-administration-plus-proche-et-plus-intelligente/>). That is [up from 605 at the end of 2023, as counted by the Court of Audit](<https://www.hespress.com/%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85%D9%86%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AE%D8%AF%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%85%D9%88%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9-1814104.html>). In the last twelve months, from 9 November 2026, [Moroccans abroad can apply online for criminal record certificates](<https://en.hespress.com/148811-moroccans-abroad-can-now-apply-online-for-criminal-record-certificates.html>) through the police's Epolice portal. No source found says how users sign in to Idarati, by the national ID or one shared account, or counts its users. Operating would need one national portal or app that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

In May 2024 the Digital Governance Unit [made Torolalana a portal for transactions as well as information](<https://github.com/digital-gov-mg/torolalana-portal-releases>), integrating services of public bodies. In the last twelve months, on 31 October 2026, the anti-corruption bureau BIANCO [launched i-Fanagna for filing asset declarations remotely](<https://www.2424.mg/news/lutte-contre-la-corruption-le-bianco-lance-i-fanagna-une-plateforme-numerique-de-declaration-de-patrimoine>). In November 2026 the higher education ministry [opened e-Courrier for submitting and tracking mail online](<https://www.2424.mg/transformation-numerique-le-ministere-de-lenseignement-superieur-ambitionne-de-traiter-90-des-courriers-sur-la-nouvelle-plateforme-e-courrier>). No source found says how many services can be completed on Torolalana, how users sign in, or how many use it. Establishing would need ten or more government services that can be completed online.

On 19 July 2024 the President [launched the digitalisation of public services](<https://bamada.net/nouvelles-technologies-le-president-de-la-transition-lance-la-digitalisation-des-moyens-de-paiement-et-des-services-publics-de-letat>). ID card fees, police fines and civil-status acts can be paid by mobile phone, first in Bamako. No source found says how users sign in to the Citizen Portal. None counts its users. Operating would need one national portal that carries services of several ministries, with sign-in by the national ID or one shared account.

In October 2026 a Mauritanian official [put the transactional services online at about forty, of nearly 900 targeted](<https://transcontinents.africa/fr/article/e-gouvernance-le-benin-et-la-mauritanie-a-lecole-estonienne>). No source found says one national portal carries several ministries' services with shared sign-in, or counts its users.
